DeployBot: ALERT: eu-central-1 hosted-api embeddings-route p95 3x baseline over 3m. Auto-rollback triggered but blocked by customer pin. https://dash.redwood/alerts/7265 :rotating_light:
Taylor: seeing a hard spike and rising 5xx. Manifest push ~7m ago. Auto-rollback attempted and failed due to route pin.
Nina: logs show backend deserialization errors and a small but correlated DB migration flag flip in the release. That explains why simple unpin won't fully remediate.
Taylor: if unpin won't help because codepath depends on the migration, we may need a manual rollback to the previous revision. That's higher risk for data but might be necessary. OpsLead, advise.
OpsLead: quick assessment: rollback will revert the migration flag that landed in the release; DBEng estimates a 7-minute window to run the safe rollback path with an in-place migration guard. Risk: partial writes during rollback window. Mitigations: set maintenance mode for the affected shard, pause writes, run rollback, then health-check. CSLead to prep customer advisory.
DBEng: accurate. We have an idempotent rollback procedure that flips the flag and runs a small compensating job. We'll need a controlled write-quiesce for 10m and to block live merges.
CSLead: prepare a short message to top affected tenants: one line explaining service impact, expected ETA, and that we're performing rollback to restore stability.
Taylor: what's the threshold for going from remediation -> rollback? OpsLead, can we set a 6m observation window and if p95 remains >2.5x or 5xx_rate >1.5% -> execute rollback?
OpsLead: agreed. Thresholds: 6m stable window. If conditions persist, we ship manual rollback. Also require two human approvals: OpsLead + DBEng. Notify EngOncall and Customer Success before executing.
Nina: I can attempt a mitigative patch to the routing manifest but that's uncertain. If we can get p95 to <1.5x within 4m, prefer mitigations.
DeployBot: NOTE: auto-rollback suppressed due to pinned route and migration dependency. Manual rollback request: `deployctl request-rollback --revision=2026-03-22-2145 --require-approvals=2`
Taylor: starting 6m observation window now. EngOncall, monitor and post screenshots every 2m. CSLead, draft the advisory. DBEng, prep the rollback playbook.
EngOncall: observation updates: 2m: p95 2.8x, 5xx 1.3%. 4m: p95 2.6x, 5xx 1.4%. 6m: p95 2.7x, 5xx 1.5%. No improvement from mitigations.
OpsLead: given the telemetry and the migration flag coupling, we are green to execute manual rollback. DBEng, please run the rollback playbook. Taylor, coordinate the ops channel and change window. CSLead, send customer advisory now.
DBEng: executing manual rollback now. Steps: set shard to maintenance, pause writes via feature-gate, run deployctl rollback --rev=2026-03-22-2145, run compensating job, health-checks for 5m, re-enable writes. Posting progress in thread.
DeployBot: Action acknowledged: manual rollback started: https://deploy.redwood/actions/726543/rollback-2026-03-22-2145
EngOncall: telemetry: after rollback initiation p95 trending down to 1.2x baseline within 3m. 5xxs falling. Continuing health checks.
DBEng: compensating job running: 1900/1900 items processed. Health checks pass. Re-enabling writes in 30s.
CSLead: advisory sent to impacted customers: "We observed elevated latency and errors in eu-central-1. We performed a targeted rollback to restore service; the issue appears resolved and metrics are returning to normal. We'll follow up with a postmortem."
OpsLead: closing change window and locking release notes. Create incident postmortem stub: https://docs.redwood/incident/726543-manual-rollback-dbflag. Great coordination, team. :thumbsup:
